dex.entry: A grey moth that drifts over sleeping kin and fans their dreams with dusty wings, so they sleep on and on. The Hollowing call it a mercy. In Stillwater the Lullwings settle on every hearth-warm heap of dozing kin and hum to them until a morning that never comes.

art.silhouette: A soft, plump moth seen from the front with its wings spread: a round furry body, feathery drooping antennae, big heavy-lidded sleepy eyes, tiny tucked legs, and broad rounded wings patterned with pale crescent-moon eye-spots. A gentle haze of silver dream-dust sifts down from the wing edges in little sparkles. At 64px it reads as a sleepy grey moth scattering moon-dust.
art.palette: Dove-grey furry body and wings shading to dusk-lilac (#6b5a8e) at the wing edges; pale moon-silver (#d8d4ec) crescent eye-spots; the dream-dust silver-white specks; the eyes deep night (#0b1026), half-lidded, one bone (#f5f0e1) highlight each; ink (#1a1430) outlines kept soft.
art.direction: Hushing, tender and a little lonely: it only wants everyone to rest. Soft, round and drowsy, a lullaby with wings, never sinister, no skulls, no fangs. Distinct from the sea-fog moth (Fogwisp): warmer grey-lilac, rounder, moon-marked, sleepy.
